approach: Recognize that the inextensible cord anchored to the wall prevents any block in the chain from moving away from the wall, no matter what F pulls on m₂.

steps.text: The cord from the wall to m₁ is inextensible and already taut, so m₁ cannot move further away from the wall.
m₂ is linked in series to m₁ through the same taut cord system, so it also cannot move away from the wall.
Apply Newton's second law to m₂ with zero acceleration: the cord tension must exactly balance the applied force F.
steps.equation: F − T = m₂(0), so T = F = 0.40 N

final_answer.value: acceleration of m₂ = 0; tension in the cord = 0.40 N

common_mistakes.text: Treating m₂ as free to accelerate under F alone, ignoring that it is linked by a taut cord back to the fixed wall, gives a₂ = 2 m/s² instead of zero.
Treating m₁ and m₂ as one combined system accelerating together under F gives a₂ = 0.8 m/s² instead of zero.
